<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide on how to translate the free5GC project’s structure and README into a clear, accurate system design diagram. Tailor the boxes, arrows, colors, and labels exactly as described for a microservice-based 5G core network.

1. Identify the project type and purpose
   • free5GC is an open-source implementation of the 5G core network (5GC) as defined by 3GPP R15.  
   • It is organized as a set of independent Network Functions (NFs) that collaborate via the Service Based Architecture (SBA).

2. Analyze the file structure
   • Top-level “NFs/” directory contains one folder per network function: AMF, SMF, UPF, NRF, UDM, UDR, AUSF, PCF, NSSF, CHF, NEF, TNGF, N3IWF.  
   • “config/” holds per-NF YAML configurations.  
   • “cert/” holds TLS certificates for each NF, implying secure HTTP/2/gRPC or REST.  
   • “webconsole/” is the UI for operations and monitoring.  
   • “test/” contains UE emulator, test packets, integration tests, and even an embedded MongoDB client—indicating that UDR uses MongoDB as the subscriber data repository.  
   • Build and orchestration scripts (Makefile, run.sh, test.sh) show that each NF runs as a standalone process, easily containerized.

3. Examine the README
   • Confirms “5G core network” and points to the online guide.  
   • Mentions nothing about a monolith—reinforcing a microservice approach.

4. Main components and their relationships
   a. Core NFs (control plane microservices)
      – AMF (Access & Mobility Management)  
      – SMF (Session Management)  
      – UPF (User Plane Function)  
      – NRF (Network Repository Function – service registry/discovery)  
      – UDM (Unified Data Management – subscriber profiles)  
      – UDR (Unified Data Repository – MongoDB)  
      – AUSF (Authentication)  
      – PCF (Policy Control)  
      – NSSF (Network Slice Selection)  
      – CHF (Charging Function)  
      – NEF (Network Exposure Function)  
      – TNGF (Transfer Gateway Function)  
      – N3IWF (Non-3GPP Interworking)  

   b. External entities
      – RAN / gNB (via NGAP to AMF)  
      – UE emulator (test/ueRanEmulator)  
      – Data Network (internet, via UPF)  
      – Web console (browser UI)  

   c. Datastore
      – MongoDB (used by UDR; other NFs may pull/push via HTTP or gRPC)  

   d. Scripts & CI
      – Orchestration scripts launch NFs in-process or containers  
      – GitHub Actions workflows for CI  

5. Architectural patterns & principles
   • Microservice-based SBA: each NF is independently deployable, communicates over secure APIs.  
   • Service discovery & registration: NRF centralizes NF endpoints.  
   • Externalization of config (YAML) and certs (PEM) for flexibility.  
   • Separation of control plane (AMF, SMF, PCF, etc.) and user plane (UPF).  
   • Use of a NoSQL store (MongoDB) for subscriber data (UDR).  
   • Web UI as a client of control plane APIs.

6. Diagram-drawing guidelines
   a. Components as boxes:
      – Control Plane NFs clustered (group by control vs. user plane).  
      – Data Plane UPF separate.  
      – External systems (RAN, UE, Data Network) at the perimeter.  
      – MongoDB icon next to UDR box.  
      – Web console & scripts grouped under “Operations / OAM.”  

   b. Relationships:
      – Directional arrows showing protocol flows:
         • UE → gNB → AMF  
         • AMF ↔ UDM/AUSF for auth  
         • AMF ↔ NRF for discovery  
         • AMF → SMF for session creation  
         • SMF → UPF (N4) for user-plane paths  
         • SMF ↔ PCF for policy rules  
         • NSSF for slice selection (AMF ↔ NSSF)  
         • NEF exposes policy/events to external application  
         • UDR ↔ UDM/PCF/CHF… (arrows to/from datastore)  
      – Web console ↔ AMF/NRF/SMF (HTTP/REST)  

   c. Color coding and shapes:
      – Control Plane NFs: blue rectangles  
      – User Plane Function (UPF): green rectangle  
      – Datastore (MongoDB): cylinder icon, colored orange  
      – External entities: gray boxes  
      – UI / Operations: purple rectangles  
      – Arrow styles: solid lines for control messages (HTTP/gRPC), dashed for data-plane (GTP/U-plane)  

   d. Labels:
      – Each arrow labeled with the protocol (e.g., NGAP, HTTP2/gRPC, N4/GTP-U)  
      – Each box labeled with NF name and port/protocol if desired  

7. Tailoring to free5GC
   • Emphasize the 3GPP SBA service links rather than generic API calls.  
   • Show “cert/” and “config/” as side artifacts (config-mount and secret-mount in containers).  
   • Optionally include a small “CI/CD” cloud icon linked to GitHub Actions workflows for completeness.  

8. Putting it all together
   • On the left: UE and RAN → arrow to AMF.  
   • Center cluster of control plane NFs in a “Core Network” box.  
   • Below, UPF connecting to “Data Network.”  
   • Right side: MongoDB datastore connected to UDR.  
   • Top: Web console connecting to AMF/NRF.  
   • Bottom: Scripts/CI icon showing orchestration and tests.

By following the above breakdown—mapping the file tree (NFs, config, certs, webconsole, test) to microservice boxes and drawing clear arrows denoting protocols—you’ll produce a comprehensive, accurate system diagram that reflects free5GC’s architecture.  
</explanation>
